body.p: This Service Level Agreement (this "SLA") is effective {{effective}} and forms part of the {{agreement}} (the "Agreement") between {{fontara_entity}} ("Vendor") and **{{customer}}**, {{customer_entity}} with its principal place of business at {{customer_address}}, {{customer_city}}, {{customer_region}} {{customer_postal}} ("Customer"). It applies to the Fontara platform subscription services under the Agreement (the "Services").

Vendor shall make the Services available at least {{uptime}} of the time in each calendar month, excluding scheduled maintenance notified under this SLA. The Services are unavailable when no user can access them.

Vendor shall give at least 5 business days' notice of scheduled maintenance and carry it out only at night or at weekends. Emergency maintenance needs at least 2 hours' notice. Scheduled maintenance carried out on notice under this section is excluded from availability.

Vendor shall respond to a Priority 1 incident (the Services are down) within 30 minutes and aim to resolve it within 4 hours, to a Priority 2 incident (a major feature is impaired with no workaround) within 2 hours and aim to resolve it within 8 hours, and to Priority 3 and 4 incidents by the next business day. Customer assigns the priority, and Vendor may reclassify an incident by written explanation within 30 minutes.

Vendor shall provide support for Priority 1 and 2 incidents 24 hours a day, every day, by phone and email, with a named path of escalation to its engineers, and for Priority 3 and 4 incidents from 9am to 6pm on business days in Vendor's local time. Each party shall name its support contacts when the Services start.
Customer support contact: [[text:Customer:Support contact name]]  Email: [[email:Customer:Support contact email]]

If availability in a month is below {{uptime}}, Vendor shall credit Customer the percentage of that month's fees for the affected Services shown in the service credit table below, against the next invoice. Customer must request a credit within 30 days after the end of the month. Credits are Customer's sole remedy for a failure to meet the availability commitment, except as the Chronic Failure section provides.

If availability falls below {{uptime}} in any three months in a rolling twelve-month period, or below 95.0% in any one month, Customer may terminate the affected Services by 30 days' written notice given within 60 days after the qualifying month, and Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after termination.

The commitments in this SLA do not apply to unavailability caused by Customer, including its misconfiguration or use beyond its limits, by a force majeure event, by the failure of a third-party service outside Vendor's reasonable control, by scheduled maintenance notified under this SLA, or by Customer's failure to apply a critical security patch Vendor recommended.

Within 5 business days after each month, Vendor shall report the month's availability, its incident log, a root cause analysis of every Priority 1 incident and any credits due. Customer may use its own independent monitoring and rely on its results in any dispute about credits.

This SLA is governed by the law that governs the Agreement, any dispute under it is resolved in the manner the Agreement provides, and notices under it are given as the Agreement provides. This SLA is the entire agreement of the parties on its subject and may be amended only in a writing signed by both parties. It may be signed in counterparts and by electronic signature, each of which is an original.
